question: If cosA = 12/13, and A is acute, find tanA.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the Pythagorean triplet involving 12 and 13.

Common triplet: (5, 12, 13), where 13 is the hypotenuse.

Given cos A = Base/Hypotenuse = 12/13.

Therefore, Perpendicular = 5.

tan A = Perpendicular/Base = 5/12.

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: cos A = 12/13, where A is acute.

Formula used: tan A = sin A / cos A or tan A = √(sec²A − 1)

 

 
 C
 A
 B
 Base (B) = 12
 P = 5
 Hypotenuse (H) = 13
 A

⇒ cos A = 12/13 = Base / Hypotenuse

⇒ By Pythagoras Theorem: (Hypotenuse)² = (Perpendicular)² + (Base)²

⇒ 13² = P² + 12²

⇒ 169 = P² + 144

⇒ P² = 169 − 144 = 25

⇒ P = √25 = 5

⇒ tan A = Perpendicular / Base = 5/12

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin²A + cos²A = 1 and 1 + tan²A = sec²A.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common right-triangle side ratios are (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

Reciprocal Ratios

sec A = 1/cos A, cosec A = 1/sin A, and cot A = 1/tan A.</p
